brique._comment: Engine-native Matter family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: matter.clone
objective.description: Clone one existing local matter into a new local target matter.

#root.role: Resolve a source matter and a target matter identifier, duplicate the descriptor and compatible substance state, and register the cloned target in the local catalog.

source_matter_id._comment: Required. Name of the source matter within the addressed context.

target_matter_id._comment: Optional. Name of the clone. Auto-generated if absent.

destination_ctx_id._comment: Optional. Absolute context path (from /root) for the clone. Defaults to the addressed context.

effects.source_descriptor: The source matter descriptor is read.
effects.source_substance: Brique-managed source substance may be read and copied.
effects.target_descriptor: A new target matter descriptor is written.
effects.catalog: The local matter catalog gains the cloned target.

transformation_contract.morphing: A source matter identity plus a target matter identity becomes a new committed target matter carrying the cloned descriptor and compatible local substance semantics.
invariants: When cloning within the same context (no destination_ctx_id, or destination_ctx_id equal to the addressed context), source_matter_id and target_matter_id must identify distinct matters.
When cloning to a different context, source_matter_id and target_matter_id may be identical, since the destination context is a distinct namespace.
The source matter must already exist in the local runtime catalog before cloning begins.
Only brique-managed substance is duplicated as bytes; non-brique substance modes remain metadata-only at clone time.
success: On success, matter.clone returns ok=true, the source_matter_id, and the concrete target_matter_id.
Successful cloning writes a new target matter descriptor, registers the target in the local catalog, and reproduces a brique-mode data.bin when applicable.
failure: The capacity fails when source_matter_id is missing.
The capacity fails when source_matter_id and target_matter_id are identical and the clone is within the same context.
The capacity refuses cloning when the source matter is absent or the destination matter_id already exists in the runtime catalog.
The capacity fails when the source descriptor is unreadable, invalid JSON, or when destination filesystem commits fail.
notes: If target_matter_id is omitted, the engine generates a fresh local destination identifier.
If destination_ctx_id is provided, the clone is written into that context instead of the addressed context; the destination context must already exist.
Cloning does not dereference wrapper-managed external substance.
